$comment: GENERATED by tools/earth/relief.py - do not edit. Every layer is on the same plate pixels as docs/map/<map>.svg, so any set of them can be stacked as they are. Order is bottom to top.
name: The Mediterranean

grid.centreOfHex: x = originX + hexAcrossPx * (col + 0.5 * (row & 1)) + hexAcrossPx / 2;  y = originY + rowPitchPx * row + hexRadiusPx

georeference.pixelToDegrees: lon = lon0 + (x - originX - hexAcrossPx / 2) / hexAcrossPx * hexLon;  lat = lat0 - (y - originY - hexRadiusPx) / rowPitchPx * rowLat
georeference.degreesToPixel: x = originX + hexAcrossPx / 2 + (lon - lon0) / hexLon * hexAcrossPx;  y = originY + hexRadiusPx + (lat0 - lat) / rowLat * rowPitchPx
georeference.projection: equirectangular, true at the standard parallel; ground distances drift from the true figure away from it

layers.role: white is land, black is sea. Sea is water joined to the open ocean, so land below sea level is land
colour only: height and depth tints, with dry ground where the climate is arid. No shading, nothing else
relief shading on its own; multiply it over any colour. 8-bit grey: factor = value / 255 x 2, so 128 is no change
the finished relief: ground-flat x shade, with the coast and rivers drawn on
the shoreline as a transparent line
river centre lines, Natural Earth scale rank 5 and above (more than the board keeps)
the game grid: a three-tone shift, then a pale line with a dark one beside it. Groups: tone, keyline-pale, keyline-dark
latitude and longitude every 5 degrees, heavier every 10, and the Tropic of Cancer
settlements at their hex, with names
paper band, neat line and degree labels

sources.name: Terrain Tiles (terrarium), zoom 7
sources.credit: SRTM, GEBCO, ETOPO1 and national datasets, as credited by Mapzen/Tilezen terrain tiles

sources.name: Natural Earth 1:10m rivers and lake centerlines
